descriptionChirho: Of waters rising and overflowing their banks or bounds; to flood, surge, pour forth abundantly, used both literally of rivers and metaphorically of overwhelming forces.
Of floodwaters or overwhelming forces sweeping over, carrying away, or engulfing persons or things; the destructive transitive effect of rushing water upon its object.
To rinse or wash an object with water, typically in a ritual or domestic context such as cleansing vessels, sacrificial items, or the body.
Niphal passive: to be rinsed or washed with water, used of objects requiring ritual cleansing.

labelChirho: be swept away (Niphal passive of flood)
descriptionChirho: Niphal passive: to be swept away or overwhelmed by flooding waters; the passive counterpart of the transitive 'sweep away' sense.
Pual intensive passive: to be thoroughly rinsed or washed, indicating a more intensive or complete washing action than the simple Niphal.
